Verticals, board · recording of 3 October 2026: 25 seconds, 15 clicks · select any words to leave a comment

One click on the board plays as two to four jerks. It should be one movement

The recording is blurred, and the card titles and notes are replaced with neutral ones, so the owner’s plans stay private.

In each of the 15 clicks something changes in one frame, 16 ms. Neighbouring cards jump 130–315 px and then take another 200–300 ms to travel the rest. The wide column moves in one frame. Twice the clicked card slides more than 550 px out from under the cursor, and 370 ms later it jumps back. Once, everything in a column vanishes for one frame.

The cause shows in the code: one click starts up to five separate mechanisms. They have different starts, durations from 40 to 600 ms and four different curves. The column width, the type size and part of the scroll change with no animation at all.

Below, each transition is shown twice in the same place: “Now” is the recording, “Fixed” is a mockup of the same screen in the board’s font, colours and sizes. In the mockup all parts of a click start in the same frame, travel for 360 ms on the curve large, which the product already has, and stop together. The ¼ and ⅒ buttons slow down both the recording and the mockup. You can click the cards in the mockup yourself.

The main rule: one click, one movement

Five fixes cover almost all the jerks in the recording. Each follows from the motion skill and from what the code does now.

  1. One driver per click. The FLIP move (moveFamily) becomes the only mechanism. Scrolling, holding the place and returning the column are computed before the second measurement and travel by the same transform rather than a separate loop on scrollTop.
  2. Nothing in one frame. The column width, the type size 12 ↔ 24, the box’s header, “14 more”, the veil and the family highlight change within the same movement. Only transform, opacity and clip-path animate; height changes only on a coloured shape with no children.
  3. The clicked card stays put if it fits. This rule comes from Kirill’s PR, and it is already in main. If the card doesn’t fit or can’t be held, it travels to its place in one pass within the same movement, with no jump back.
  4. What leaves fades out in place; what arrives travels in with everything else. The closed part fades out in 150 ms under whatever slides over it. Returning plans start a quarter of the way into the movement and stop in the same frame as the rest.
  5. Hovering doesn’t change the layout and doesn’t flicker. The lift of the card under the hand stays instant: it answers the hand. After a click, hover waits until the hand moves, so content that slid under the cursor isn’t highlighted. I suggest turning the family highlight on after the hand rests for 250 ms; the decision is yours, and it’s at the end.

A card’s path, frame by frame: now a step and a settle; it should be one curve

The position of one line of text, found in every frame of the recording (60 frames per second), against the same path in one movement: 360 ms on the curve large, the same start and the same finish. The vertical axis runs like the screen: down means down.

Now, a dot per frameFixed, one movement
The numbers as a table

Switching inside a column: the neighbour jumps 315 px in one frame, then travels the rest

“Style guide” is open; we click “Page 5” above it. In the frame at 3.650 s the text of “Style guide” disappears entirely, and its title jumps down 315 px. It travels the remaining 121 px in 200 ms on a different curve. At 4.75 s the same happens to “Page 5”: 219 px in one frame, then 197 px with a one-frame stop in the middle.

This happens because the FLIP move measures positions before the scroll, and then a separate Glide runs the scroll on its own curve. Nothing animates part of the path, and that part passes in one frame. In the mockup, closing and opening are one movement: “Page 5” opens downward under its title, and “Style guide” collapses and moves down exactly with the edge of the opening card.

The clicked card slides out from under the cursor and jumps back 370 ms later

“Page 1” is open; we click “Style guide” near the bottom edge. In the first frame it jumps up 263 px, then travels another 308 px up, towards the top of the column. At 370 ms after the click (the frame at 2.433 s) everything jumps back down 152 px. Meanwhile “Reply to the forum” slides in under the motionless cursor and lights up grey, although nobody touched it.

The same at 7.60 s: “Page 1” moves up 553 px, and exactly 370 ms later the column jumps back 85 px. A similar tail shows when a plan opens in the box: after 350 ms the open card loses 62 px of empty space at the bottom in one frame (11.93 s). The likely cause in the code: while the notes open for 360 ms, Glide and the card itself treat it as taller than it will be. When the animation ends, the extra height vanishes in one frame, and the browser clamps the scroll. This hasn’t been checked by running the app.

Here “Style guide” can’t be held in place: a long card closes above it, and the column is scrolled by only 54 px. Kirill’s rule says: if the card doesn’t fit, the column scrolls exactly as far as it takes to show it whole. In the mockup this rule is met in one pass. The card rises once and comes to rest, there is no jump back, and hover doesn’t light up until the hand moves.

The carried box: the list jumps 160 px up, then gets pushed 448 down

We click the first plan in the “17 from Sep” box. In the frame at 11.583 s the two other plans and “14 more” vanish, the box snaps shut, and the list under it jumps up 160 px. Over the next 283 ms the opening plan pushes the same list down 448 px. The eye sees a jerk there and back. The plan itself is pale for these 200 ms, under the veil, and turns bright in one frame. And 350 ms after the click the card also loses 62 px of empty space at the bottom, and the list jumps up again.

The third plan (18.0 s) jumps 130 px up to the header in one frame, travels 30 px more, and then jitters 1–2 px back and forth for 250 ms: two mechanisms pull it, each towards its own place. On closing via the header (10.2 s) the list jumps up 162 px and travels 60 px more with a one-frame stop.

In the mockup the box collapses to its header line in the same movement. The other plans fade out in place under the opening card, the clicked plan rises to the header in one pass, and the header’s backing fades in along with everything. On closing, the plans come out from under the line and fall into place in the same frame as the list.

The wide column moves in one frame, and the open card assembles in three steps over another 180 ms

A plan is open in Week; we click “Prepare for the Monday call” in Month. All the steps of one click are visible separately:

In the code, the column width and the font sizes switch by a class with no transition; width transitions exist only in the 3D mode, which is turned off. The wide column is the same column, closer: the type size exactly doubles, 12 → 24 px. So in the mockup Month zooms in around the clicked card, and Week moves away. The plan’s backing grows into the open card, its title moves and grows, and the column’s name slides along with its left edge. All of this is one movement of 360 ms; no step waits for another.

In Quarter one frame is empty, and the “Review the pricing page…” line lies over the text for five frames

Switching between “Deliver the onboarding redesign…” and its step “Write the onboarding checklist…” in Quarter (22.23 and 23.25 s). The causes are the same as in the first section, but two new glitches show.

Text over text appears when the new card’s steps come in with no transition while its notes open via the grid 0fr → 1fr over 360 ms. The empty frame is the moment when the old parts are already removed and the copies of the new ones aren’t drawn yet. The cure is the same rule as in the first section: one measured height, the parts open with clip-path in the same movement, what leaves fades out in place.

The family highlight chases the hand: at every card on the way, three columns repaint

The hand heads for “Prepare for the Monday call” in Month and on the way brushes “Validate the beta…” for 33 ms. The family highlight in Year, 3 years and Life switches to its family in one frame, and two frames later to the right one.

At 19.97 s the hand passes through Quarter, and the open card in Month dims for two frames while the family in Quarter lights up. After 33 ms the card is bright again. The eye sees a flash where it wasn’t looking.

I suggest this rule for hovering. The lift of the card under the hand stays instant: it answers the hand. The family highlight comes on or switches only when the hand stays on one card for 250 ms; the box already has this rule, and it should be extended to the whole board. The highlight comes on in 150 ms and fades out in 300. Hovering never moves the layout. In the mockups on this page hover works the same way, only without the family highlight: the mockups don’t draw the neighbouring columns.

I didn’t find in the code why the open card stays pale, under the veil, for 180–200 ms after the click and lights up in one frame (8.70 and 11.78 s). This should be checked separately.

Gemini’s report: the overall picture is right; I rechecked the details frame by frame

Gemini 3.8 Flash watched the recording slowed down 20 times with the frame number on each frame, the recording at real speed, two frame-by-frame sheets and the full text of our motion skill. It sees roughly one frame per second, that is, every third frame of the recording. Everything this page takes from its report has been checked against the frame-by-frame track.

Confirmed

  • The column switch breaks into three steps: 8.517, 8.567 and about 8.7 s.
  • The empty frame in Quarter, 23.267 s.
  • The clicked card runs away from under the cursor (2.07, 15.5 and 18.0 s); the false hover on “Reply to the forum”.
  • Almost every change starts with a one-frame jump; what’s needed is one movement, FLIP and only transform and opacity.

Wrong

  • “React”, scrollIntoView, setActiveColumn are made up: the board is built on Vue, and the mechanisms are Move, Glide, scrollBack and holdPlace (the code section).
  • 8.717 s: the card doesn’t jump 32 px. At 8.700 s it turns bright in one frame, and the header’s backing appears.
  • 3.65 s: “Style guide” jumps down 315 px, not up.
  • 10.2 s: the list jumps up 162 px, not down 180.
  • 2.433 s: the jump back is 152 px, not ~50.
  • The “flex-basis/width transition” advice for the column switch contradicts the skill: the text would rewrap every frame. Instead, the mockup has a zoom with a swap of renderings.

Missed

  • Almost every move is a step and a settle: after the jump, another 200–300 ms on a different curve, sometimes with a one-frame stop.
  • The tail 350–370 ms after the click: the column jumps back 85 px (7.97 s), the card loses 62 px of empty space (11.93 s).
  • The open card stays pale for 180–200 ms and lights up in one frame (11.78 s).
  • Text over text in Quarter, 22.25–22.32 s, and the third plan’s jitter at 18.1 s.
  • The family highlight jumps to another family for 33 ms (7.917 s); the open card blinks at 19.97 s.

Anatomical analysis of motion in the Horizons interface and a fix plan

This document is a step-by-step, frame-by-frame breakdown of a recording of the app at work (the files board-slow20x.mp4, board-realtime.mp4, the contact sheets frames-plan-switch-1.97-2.60s.png and frames-column-switch-8.27-8.85s.png) in strict accordance with the laws of interface physics and the rules of motion-skill.md.

All timestamps and frame numbers are given solely in the real time of the original recording (60 fps), shown on the yellow bar at the bottom of the video.

1. The foundation of meaning: what every motion must say

The interface must convey five key meanings: 1. Opening in place (Open in place): A click opens the card right where it was: it smoothly unfolds into its full form (title, body with the description, documents, the “Discuss with agent” block) and stays under the pointer. 2. Focus column (Open column): The column with the open card widens, getting a larger type size; the neighbouring columns make room for it. 3. Closing the previous goal: Opening a new card folds the previously open one back into a compact one-line bar. 4. Carried-over plans in the tinted box: Tasks from past periods are grouped in a bar (for example, “17 from Sep · Replan”). When one of them opens, the whole box collapses into a header line, and the open goal stands directly under it; the header serves as the point of return to the list. 5. Family links (Family tint): Parent goals in the right-hand (long-term) columns and child goals in the left-hand ones are highlighted in a soft green tone. When the card changes, the highlight moves to the new family in sync.

2. Frame-by-frame breakdown of every transition (all 15 clicks)

Transition 1: Week column — Card switch from “Page 1” to “Style guide for the team”

  • Real time and frames: 1.967s – 2.600s (f118 – f156). Click at f124–f125 (2.067s – 2.083s).
  • Anatomy (The bones):
  • Before the click (f118–f124): “Page 1” is open at the top of the Week column. Below it, “Page 5”, “Style guide for the team” and “Reply to the forum” are closed. The cursor moves down and clicks on “Style guide for the team”.
  • Phase 1 (f126, 2.100s, exactly 1 frame after the click) [SEEN]:
    • “Page 1” instantly collapses its body into one line in 0 ms (no animation).
    • The “Page 5” card teleports up by ~220 px.
    • The “Style guide for the team” card teleports up by ~220 px, the title font abruptly grows, the background abruptly floods with green, the card body is mounted.
    • Position under the cursor: The “Style guide” card instantly flies up out from under the cursor! The cursor is left hanging over an empty area at the bottom of the open body (over the “64 more lines” row).
  • Phase 2 (f128, 2.133s, 33 ms / 2 frames later) [SEEN]:
    • A sudden scroll jump upward! “Page 1” disappears completely past the top edge of the viewport. The “Page 5” card ends up pressed against the top edge.
  • Phase 3 (f132, 2.200s, 100 ms later) [SEEN]:
    • False hover: the lower card “Reply to the forum” shifted under the motionless cursor and suddenly turned the dark grey hover colour.
  • Phase 4 (f146, 2.433s, 330 ms after the click!) [SEEN]:
    • A sudden convulsive jump of the layout downward! “Page 1” jerks back into the visible area at the top. “Page 5”, “Style guide” and all the elements below are thrown down by ~50 px.
  • Stabilisation: f150–f156 (2.500s – 2.600s).
  • Violations of motion-skill.md:
  • “Transform and opacity” — Deadly gross violation (severe) [SEEN]: geometry changes and collapsing via a synchronous reflow/layout in 0 frames instead of composite layers.
  • “The ground stays still: no neighbour snaps 16 px in one frame, and no container jumps 20 px” — Gross violation (severe) [SEEN]: the neighbours jumped by >200 px in 1 frame.
  • “A click opens the card in place... and stays where it was clicked, under the pointer” — Gross violation (severe) [SEEN]: the goal popped out from under the hand.
  • “Hover lifts only what the click takes” — Noticeable violation (noticeable) [SEEN]: a parasitic hover on the neighbouring card “Reply to the forum” because of content moving under the cursor.
  • “Kill parasitic motion... in three steps where one would do” — Gross violation (severe) [SEEN]: one click caused three separate jerks of the screen at f126, f128 and f146.
  • Failure mechanism: Synchronous render of the new state in React/DOM -> zeroing of the old card's height -> 2 frames later a belated scrollIntoView() fires -> 330 ms later a deferred height correction of the parent container or the sticky header fires.
  • Meaning: Meaning 1 is completely destroyed. The eye sees an elevator falling on a snapped cable, a double shove of the screen and a loss of visual focus.
  • Fix in values:
  • The “Style guide” card must stay strictly under the cursor: its top edge keeps its screen coordinate.
  • “Page 1” smoothly folds up via a FLIP transform (height via a container with overflow: hidden, height: auto is animated via FLIP transform: translateY + scaleY), duration 250 ms, curve cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1).
  • The column scroll is synchronised in the same animation frame, with no repeated jumps.

Transition 2: Week column — Card switch from “Style guide” to “Page 5”

  • Real time and frames: 3.617s – 3.800s (f217 – f228). Click at f218–f219 (3.633s – 3.650s).
  • Anatomy (The bones):
  • Before the click (f217): The cursor moves onto the one-line card “Page 5 · The inbox: final draft”, located directly above the expanded “Style guide”.
  • Phase 1 (f220, 3.667s) [SEEN]: In 1 frame, “Style guide” collapses into a one-liner. “Page 5” unfolds its body. The lower cards jump up.
  • Phase 2 (f223–f226, 3.717s – 3.767s) [SEEN]: A micro-shift of the scroll by 4–6 px.
  • Violations of motion-skill.md:
  • “Transform and opacity” (severe) [SEEN]: an abrupt replacement of the DOM with no intermediate frames.
  • “Clean middle frames” (noticeable) [SEEN]: instant re-wrapping of the text lines.
  • “The ground stays still” (severe) [SEEN]: an instant leap of the neighbours below.
  • Mechanism: An instant swap of state classes in the DOM.
  • Meaning: Meaning 3 (smooth folding) does not read; the cards twitch like frames in a broken projector.
  • Fix: The height of “Page 5” unfolds from 40 px to full, while “Style guide” shrinks at the same time, over 250 ms on the curve cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1).

Transition 3: Week column — Card switch from “Page 5” to “Page 1”

  • Real time and frames: 4.717s – 4.867s (f283 – f292). Click at f284–f285 (4.733s – 4.750s).
  • Anatomy (The bones):
  • The cursor clicks on the folded “Page 1” line at the top.
  • Phase 1 (f286, 4.767s) [SEEN]: In one frame, “Page 1” expands downward, pushing “Page 5” and “Style guide” down by 300+ px. The green family bars in Month/Quarter/Year abruptly switch to the new branch.
  • Violations of motion-skill.md:
  • “The ground stays still” (severe) [SEEN]: the lower part of the column drops by a third of the screen in 16 ms.
  • “a colour change takes a gentle ease” (noticeable) [SEEN]: an instant change in the colour of the family links.
  • Mechanism: Layout reflow in one frame.
  • Meaning: The eye reads a blow from top to bottom (a “piston”), instead of a document opening.
  • Fix: A downward FLIP shift of the “Page 5” card and the ones below, with smooth deceleration (250 ms, cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)), and the “Page 1” body appearing via opacity: 0 -> 1 (150 ms).

Transition 4: Week column — Card switch from “Page 1” to “Page 3”

  • Real time and frames: 6.117s – 6.267s (f367 – f376). Click at f368–f369 (6.133s – 6.150s).
  • Anatomy (The bones):
  • The cursor clicks in the area above “Page 1” (on the header or a hidden element of the carried-over plans).
  • Phase 1 (f370, 6.167s) [SEEN]: At the very top of the column, a giant open card “Page 3 · Sharing a project: final draft” materialises. The whole column shifts down by 380 px.
  • Violations of motion-skill.md:
  • “Back the way it came / An entrance starts near full size... never from zero” (severe) [SEEN]: the element appeared out of nowhere, with no trajectory.
  • “The ground stays still” (severe) [SEEN]: a catastrophic shift of the whole working area.
  • Mechanism: Mounting a new node in the DOM without an animated container.
  • Fix: If the card was in a folded box, the box smoothly spreads open and the card emerges from its original position.

Transition 5: Week column — Card switch from “Page 3” to “Page 1”

  • Real time and frames: 7.567s – 7.733s (f454 – f464). Click at f456–f457 (7.600s).
  • Anatomy (The bones):
  • A click on the folded “Page 1” bar.
  • Phase 1 (f458, 7.633s) [SEEN]: “Page 3” instantly disappears, “Page 1” instantly opens.
  • Violations: Identical to transitions 1–3 (zero duration, abrupt reflow).

Transition 6: Switching the active column — A click from Week into Month on “Prepare for the Monday call”

  • Real time and frames: 8.267s – 8.850s (f496 – f531). Click at f510 (8.500s). Full confirmation on the contact sheet frames-column-switch-8.27-8.85s.png.
  • Anatomy (The bones) — the multi-phase break-up of a single action:
  • Before the click (f496–f509): Week is wide (~340 px), Month is narrow (~180 px). In Month the cards are shown in small type, squeezed in width. The cursor aims at “Prepare for the Monday call”.
  • Phase 1 (f511, 8.517s, +16 ms after the click) [SEEN]:
    • The Week column instantly shrinks from 340 px to 180 px!
    • The Month column instantly widens from 180 px to 340 px!
    • The Quarter, Year, 3 years and Life columns instantly shift right by ~160 px!
    • The text in all columns instantly re-wraps its lines (re-wrap).
    • But the “Prepare for the Monday call” card is still CLOSED! It has simply become wider.
  • Phase 2 (f514, 8.567s, +67 ms after the click / +50 ms after Phase 1) [SEEN]:
    • The “Prepare for the Monday call” card suddenly flings its body open!
    • The lower cards (“Check the reminders...”) come crashing down by 350 px.
    • The card sits right under the “Month” label.
  • Phase 3 (f523, 8.717s, +217 ms after the click / +150 ms after the body opened!) [SEEN]:
    • Suddenly, ABOVE the open card, the grey line “17 from Sep · Replan” materialises!
    • The whole expanded card, with all its content, jumps down by ~32 px!
    • The green family-link marks in Quarter and Year update with a delay.
  • Stabilisation: f528–f531 (8.800s – 8.850s).
  • Violations of motion-skill.md:
  • “One movement: Everything one action changes moves as one: the same axis, duration and easing, ending together” — Extremely gross violation (severe) [SEEN]: one user action fell apart into three independent visual explosions, 50 and 150 ms apart!
  • “Transform and opacity: animating width, height... lays it out on every frame, and a text box that changes width makes words jump from line to line” — Gross violation (severe) [SEEN]: an instant jump of the column widths and the text breaking apart.
  • “The ground stays still: no container jumps 20 px” — Gross violation (severe) [SEEN]: the neighbouring columns jumped by 160 px, the cards down by 350 px, then by 32 px.
  • “Kill parasitic motion” — (severe) [SEEN]: a triple desync.
  • Failure mechanism:
  • setActiveColumn('Month') fires in frame 511.
  • setOpenCard('monday_call') renders through an async cycle in frame 514.
  • The carried-over group's hook/selector works out membership in “17 from Sep” and mounts the header only in frame 523!
  • Meaning: Meaning 2 (“The column smoothly makes room”) and Meaning 4 (“The box folds into the header, the goal stands under it”) do not work. The eye sees an epileptic interface failure in which the screen jerks three times in different directions.
  • Fix in values:
  • All three changes must be merged into one synchronous transaction lasting 250 ms.
  • Column width change: a synchronous flex-basis / width transition on the curve cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1).
  • The “17 from Sep · Replan” header is already present in the DOM at t=0 and does not jump.
  • The card body expands at the same time as the column widens, not 150 ms after.

Transition 7: Month column — Closing the card into the list of the tinted box

  • Real time and frames: 10.167s – 10.267s (f610 – f616). Click at f611–f612 (10.183s – 10.200s).
  • Anatomy (The bones):
  • A click on the “17 from Sep · Replan” line at the top.
  • Phase 1 (f613, 10.217s) [SEEN]: In 1 frame, the open card “Prepare for the Monday call” collapses into a one-liner. Inside the bar, two more lines instantly appear: “Validate the beta...” and “Invite beta testers”, plus the “14 more” bar.
  • All the tasks below, outside the box, jump down by ~180 px.
  • Violations: “Transform and opacity” (severe), “The ground stays still” (severe) [SEEN].
  • Mechanism: Conditional rendering {isOpen ? <SingleCard/> : <FullList/>} with no animation of height and opacity.
  • Meaning: Meaning 4 (“The header line is the way back to the list”) works logically, but visually the list explodes instantly.
  • Fix: Revealing the hidden list items via a cascading opacity (0 -> 1 over 150 ms) with a simultaneous smooth increase of the box height over 200 ms.

  • Violations of motion-skill.md:
  • “A click opens the card in place... and stays where it was clicked, under the pointer” — Gross violation (severe) [SEEN]: the card teleported from the second position to the first, breaking away from the hand that clicked!
  • “The ground stays still” (severe) [SEEN].
  • Mechanism: The template logic renders the open card strictly at a fixed position under the group header, ignoring its physical position in the list.
  • Meaning: Meanings 1 and 4 are grossly distorted. The user sees the object jump upward and a loss of footing.

Transition 15: Quarter column — Return to “checklist” with a visual glitch (Flash of Empty Content)

  • Real time and frames: 23.217s – 23.367s (f1393 – f1402). Click at f1394–f1395 (23.233s – 23.250s).
  • Anatomy (The bones):

    • In frame 1396, all the cards inside Quarter disappear completely!
    • An absolutely empty green rectangular block renders on screen between the “17 from Q3 · Replan” line and the lower goal “Review the pricing page...”.
    • No text, no buttons, no dividers — a visual “hole” in the interface.
  • Phase 2 (f1399, 23.317s, 50 ms later) [SEEN]:

  • Violations of motion-skill.md:
  • “Solid to the end: Nothing pops in front of another mid-motion... things at rest don't pass through each other” — Extreme defect (severe) [SEEN]: the content drops out completely for 1–2 frames.
  • “Clean middle frames” (severe) [SEEN].
  • Failure mechanism: Unmounting the previous card before the next one's DOM is ready (a race condition in React/the component), or a reset of the list's key, which caused all the nodes to be re-created.
  • Meaning: The meaning of the physical object's integrity is completely destroyed. The interface flashes a broken field of pixels.
  • Fix: Keeping stable DOM keys, a smooth crossfade of the content with no intermediate unmounting of the container.

3. Summary table of violations of the motion-skill.md laws

Element Exact wording of the law from motion-skill.md Severity Status
Board columns “Transform and opacity: animating width, height... lays it out on every frame, and a text box that changes width makes words jump from line to line” Severe SEEN (f511, f1252)
Neighbouring cards “The ground stays still: no neighbour snaps 16 px in one frame, and no container jumps 20 px” Severe SEEN (all transitions)
Clicked card “A click opens the card in place... and stays where it was clicked, under the pointer” Severe SEEN (f126, f931, f1081)
Column switch “One movement: Everything one action changes moves as one: the same axis, duration and easing, ending together” Severe SEEN (f511 -> f514 -> f523)
Parasitic scroll “Kill parasitic motion... in three steps where one would do” Severe SEEN (f126 -> f128 -> f146)
Empty frame in Quarter “Solid to the end: Nothing pops in front of another mid-motion” / “Clean middle frames” Severe SEEN (f1396)
Family highlight “a colour change takes a gentle ease” / “When a set changes, show what went where” Noticeable SEEN (all transitions)
Hover on cards “Hover lifts only what the click takes” (false hover from the content shift) Noticeable SEEN (f132)
Animation curves “Ease out, never in... cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)” (no interpolation) Severe SEEN (0 ms everywhere)

4. Root causes (Root Causes) of the visual roughness

  1. Discrete instant Layout Switch (0 ms): The app changes CSS classes and state in one frame. Neither the column width nor the card height is interpolated over time.
  2. Lifecycle desynchronisation (Multi-step Async Cascades): One user intent (a click) is split into 2–3 independent state effects with different timings: first the column, then the body unfolding, then the group header.
  3. Belated scroll auto-correction (scrollIntoView): An imperative scroll is called asynchronously after the DOM update, causing a convulsive rebound of the already redrawn screen.
  4. Loss of the spatial anchor (Spatial Anchor Loss): Expanding a card inside the carried-over list always moves it to a fixed top position instead of expanding it where it was clicked.
  5. Flicker on component remount (Unmount Flash): Internal state is reset along with the destruction of DOM nodes, producing empty frames (f1396).

5. Prioritised fix plan (Biggest Effect First)

Priority 1: Eliminate the split of transitions into several steps (One Movement)

  • What to do: Merge the column width change, the card expansion and the display of the “17 from Sep” group into a single indivisible state transaction. Forbid the deferred rendering of the carried-overheader.
  • Effect: The triple convulsive jerk of the screen on a column switch will disappear (f511 -> f514 -> f523).

Priority 2: Implement opening in place (Open in Place) via FLIP

  • What to do: When a card is clicked, record its screen Y coordinate via getBoundingClientRect(). On expanding, the card grows from this point instead of jumping up. The neighbouring elements slide apart using CSS transform: translateY(...).
  • Effect: The card stays under the finger/cursor; the feeling of “the rug being pulled out” disappears.

Priority 3: Animating column width without redrawing the text at every pixel

  • What to do: Run the column width transition over 250 ms on the curve cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1). To avoid constant abrupt word wrapping (re-wrapping) during the motion, the content of the new wide column is rendered at the target width right away, inside a container with a fixed width and an animated clip-path / transform: scaleX, or with a smooth crossfade preview -> full form.
  • Effect: The text jitter and the false hovers disappear.

Priority 4: Get rid of the parasitic auto-scroll

  • What to do: Remove the desynchronised scrollIntoView() calls after render. If a scroll is needed, compute the delta in advance and animate scrollTop in the same rAF loop as the card's FLIP transform.
  • Effect: The secondary and tertiary layout jerks are eliminated (as at f128 and f146).

Priority 5: Smooth transfer of the family highlight (Family Tint)

  • What to do: Add a CSS transition of the background colour: transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1). When the goal changes, the old bars softly fade out and the new ones softly light up.
  • Effect: The links are read by peripheral vision without a strobe effect.

6. Target timelines of the reference motion (0, 16, 50, 100, 150, 250 ms)

Type 1: Opening in place inside the tinted box (Open in place in tinted box)

Goal: A card inside the box of carried-over plans has been clicked. The box smoothly folds into the header line, the selected goal stands under it and opens its details.

 0 ms (Click): Card pressed. Pressed look (scale 0.98, background highlight).
16 ms:       Animation start. The neighbouring cards in the box begin to dissolve (opacity: 1 -> 0).
             The box header begins to slide toward the compact line “17 from Sep · Replan”.
50 ms:       The unselected cards have dissolved by 50%.
             The selected card begins to open the details block (opacity: 0, clip-path opening up).
             The board's lower tasks smoothly shift down via transform: translateY.
100 ms:      The neighbouring cards are fully hidden (opacity: 0).
             The box header has locked into its compact form.
             The selected card has reached 70% of its expansion.
150 ms:      The card body (text, documents) has faded in to 90% (opacity: 1).
             The shift of the lower cards slows down (ease-out).
250 ms:      Full rest (At rest). The card stands strictly under the header line. 
             No corrective scrolls or bounces.

Type 2: Switching to another card in the same column (Card Switch in same column)

Goal: One card is open; we click another. The old one folds into a one-liner, the new one opens.

 0 ms (Click): Instant response to the press.
16 ms:       The previously open card begins to collapse its details (the body's opacity drops).
             The clicked card begins to enlarge its title and widen its container.
             The clicked card's title coordinate smoothly slides to the new position.
50 ms:       The old card's body is gone. The containers change height in sync on a shared FLIP driver.
100 ms:      The old card has fully turned into a one-liner.
             The new card has expanded 80% of its body height.
150 ms:      The new card's body is fully visible (opacity: 1, the text stable, no jumps).
250 ms:      Full rest (At rest). The grid is stable, the cursor exactly over the open goal.

Type 3: Switching the active column (Column Switch)

Goal: A click on a card in a narrow column. This column becomes wide, and the previous one narrow.

 0 ms (Click): Instant lock-in of the intent. Highlight on the clicked card's title.
16 ms:       Both columns start moving their widths in sync on a single easing token.
             Wide column: 340 px -> 180 px. Narrow column: 180 px -> 340 px.
             The content of the shrinking column smoothly turns into its compact form.
50 ms:       90% of the column width shift is complete (thanks to the curve cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)).
             The body of the opening card begins to fade in.
100 ms:      The column widths have reached their target values.
             The neighbouring columns on the right smoothly slow their horizontal shift.
150 ms:      The open card's body is 100% visible.
250 ms:      Full rest (At rest). All columns are still, the typography is locked.

Type 4: Moving the family highlight (Family Tint Moving)

Goal: The green highlight passes from the old branch of goals to the new one.

 0 ms (Click): Lock-in of the new active branch of links.
16 ms:       The old green bars begin to smoothly lose saturation (ease-out).
             The new family cards begin to softly take on a light green tint.
50 ms:       The old bars have almost returned to the neutral colour (70% of the way).
             The new bars have gained 70% of the highlight brightness.
100 ms:      The old bars are fully neutral. The new bars have gained 95% of the colour.
150 ms:      Full rest (At rest). The highlight has softly settled on the new family of goals.

Your decisions

  1. Switching the wide column: a zoom around the clicked card, or just a border shift with a fade-in? My pick: the zoom, as in the mockup. The wide column really is the same column, closer, at exactly twice the type size; the movement explains just that.
  2. Family highlight on hover: at once, as now, or after the hand rests for 250 ms? My pick: after 250 ms, and keep the lift of the card itself instant. That way a hand crossing the board doesn’t repaint three columns at every card, and the rule matches what already works in the box.
  3. Duration: 360 ms, as now, or 260 ms? The --vt-dur-board token, 260 ms, exists but isn’t used anywhere. My pick: 360 ms on large. This value already sits in five places, 90 % of the path passes in ~120 ms, and nothing new is needed.
